title: BloombergNEF New Energy Outlook 2026: Solar to Become World's Largest Electricity Source by 2032, Storage Grows 17x
detail: BloombergNEF released its flagship New Energy Outlook 2026, finding that solar will become the world's single largest source of electricity by 2032 and that global battery storage deployment will jump 17-fold — from 223 GW in 2025 to 3.8 TW by 2035. The report found that recent energy market shocks are accelerating decoupling from imported fossil fuels globally. China's coal share of electricity is projected to fall from 54% in 2025 to just 7% by 2050. Electrification is now expanding rapidly across transport, buildings, and industry. The report marks a historic milestone: not since the age of steam has a single energy technology risen so fast to so dominant a position as solar PV in the current decade.

title: Scientists Cut Worst-Case Warming Ceiling from 4.5°C to 3.5°C — Solar and Wind Deployment Credited
detail: Leading climate scientists from the Scenario Model Intercomparison Project (ScenarioMIP) announced that the upper limit of the worst-case warming scenario has been revised down from 4.5°C to 3.5°C above pre-industrial levels by 2100. The revision directly credits the plummeting cost and rapid deployment of solar and wind power, which has made a high-fossil-fuel future increasingly implausible as a pathway. Current policy trajectory still suggests approximately 2.5°C of warming by 2100. The scientists cautioned that while the worst-case ceiling has been lowered, the best-case 1.5°C Paris Agreement target remains under threat, and urgent acceleration of the clean energy transition is still required. The findings will feed into future IPCC assessment cycles.

media.caption: Scientists revise worst-case warming ceiling down from 4.5°C to 3.5°C — renewable energy deployment credited

title: Hyundai Motor Group and 9 Partners Sign Hong Kong Green Hydrogen Ecosystem MOU — 2030 Target Set
detail: At the International Hydrogen Development Symposium 2026 in Hong Kong, ten organizations — including Hyundai Motor Company, Hyundai Engineering & Construction, JING, Towngas (HK and China Gas Co.), Veolia, and others — signed an MOU to build Hong Kong's comprehensive, self-sustaining green hydrogen ecosystem by end-2030. The agreement covers green hydrogen production from landfill biogas (waste-to-hydrogen), hydrogen fuel-cell commercial vehicles and generators, and hydrogen refueling infrastructure. The deal marks a significant expansion of Hyundai's Asia-Pacific hydrogen strategy and advances the city's decarbonization plan. Hong Kong aims to deploy 1,000+ hydrogen-powered commercial vehicles by 2030 under the agreement.
